title: A Confirmatory Paired Evaluation of Generate→Verify→Repair vs LLM‑Only NetOps Suggestions: A Reproducible Ceiling/Null Result
abstract: We preregistered (study_id=cand-002-gvr-loop) and executed a fully artifact‑archived paired experiment comparing a generate→verify→repair (G→V→R) pipeline to accepting an LLM suggestion directly for intent→configuration NetOps tasks. Using a deterministic task generator and validator, K=200 tasks were selected deterministically; a single shared generator output per task was evaluated in both arms. Observed primary outcome: baseline = 200/200 validator‑compliant applies; guarded = 200/200; paired difference = 0.00; exact McNemar two‑sided p = 1.00; paired bootstrap (10,000 resamples, seed=1729) 95% percentile CI = [0.00,0.00]. The repair step was never invoked. We release full execution and scoring artifacts (raw_results.jsonl SHA‑256 = 3dfbe1b6580c9df4...) and verifier traces to enable replay and audit. We interpret this ceiling/null outcome as specific to the tested model/task/validator regime, and we provide artifact‑grounded recommendations for future failure‑rich or interactive evaluations.

sections.introduction: Automated NetOps translation from operator intent to device configuration promises efficiency but risks service regressions (reachability loss, service interruption). A commonly proposed operational architecture is generate→verify→repair (G→V→R): an LLM proposes commands, a deterministic verifier checks safety/assurance contracts, and a repair module attempts to fix violations before apply. While prior work prototypes such pipelines and argues for their necessity, rigorous causal estimates of the verifier’s marginal value under preregistered, reproducible conditions are lacking. We designed a confirmatory paired experiment whose objective (primary estimand) is the paired_success_rate_difference_guarded_minus_baseline: the within‑task difference in binary validator pass rates when (i) the same generated candidate is accepted directly (baseline) versus (ii) the candidate is passed through verify→repair first (guarded). The experiment used a shared_initial_generation design (one generator call per task used by both arms) and deterministic selection of K=200 tasks (SHA‑256(intent_string) sort). Key archived fingerprints: raw_results.jsonl (SHA‑256 = 3dfbe1b6580c9df4...), model_configuration.json (gpt-5-mini requested; SHA‑256 = 1acce92558edeb13...), preregistration (SHA‑256 = a6d73a5c...), and the exact initial master prompt (provenance/master_prompt.txt; SHA‑256 = 1872df1e...). The run adhered to the preregistered stopping, retry, and contamination policies; no human manual manuscript editing occurred after the autonomy lock.
sections.related_work: Recent surveys and system papers position generate–validate–repair and verifier‑augmented agentic toolchains as central to trustworthy NetOps and AIOps. Benchmarks such as Cornetto evaluate LLM repair at scale and highlight regression risks when LLMs propose configuration fixes; other work (TypoNet, self‑evolving verifiers) argues for separating translation from solver‑based reasoning to obtain auditability and reliability. Our contribution differs: we provide a preregistered, artifact‑archived paired causal estimate of verifier marginality under a deterministic selection and execution contract, with all model prompts, provider traces, and validator outputs archived for replay. We cite and verify primary sources for the architectures and verification methods we discuss (see cited_record_ids).
sections.methodology:
Preregistration and design. The study preregistration (cand-002-gvr-loop; SHA‑256 = a6d73a5c...) froze: primary estimand (paired_success_rate_difference_guarded_minus_baseline), K=200 tasks, deterministic selection (SHA‑256(intent) sort), requested_model=gpt-5-mini, shared_initial_generation (one generator call per task reused by both arms), maximum_repair_calls_per_task=1, and analysis executor paired_binary_analysis_v1 with an exact McNemar test and paired bootstrap (10,000 resamples, seed=1729). The execution adapter was hosted_netops_gvr_v1.

Task generation and inclusion. A deterministic task generator (deterministic_netops_task_generator_v5) synthesized tasks with explicit workflow constraints (must_be_down_for_fields, protected_interfaces, group minima). Inclusion required the preregistered deterministic validator to report coverage for the intent; this filter is archived and reproducible (execution/task_manifest.jsonl SHA‑256 = f1d447b7...). Task selection used the lexicographic order of SHA‑256(intent_string) to avoid human selection bias.

Shared initial generation. For each task we recorded one shared_initial candidate (one generator call); the baseline arm accepted that candidate directly for validator scoring after simulated apply; the guarded arm first validated the candidate and permitted at most one repair call if validation failed. This design isolates the verifier+repair marginal effect on a fixed generator output but intentionally prevents generator adaptation to validator feedback—this is a preregistered estimand choice and is discussed as a central design constraint.

Deterministic validator and scoring. The deterministic validator (deterministic_netops_validator_v5) parses candidate commands into structured field changes, enforces workflow constraints and asset protection policies, simulates the post‑apply state snapshot, and returns a binary valid flag plus detailed diagnostics (parsed_command_count, observed_touched_field_count, final_state). Every scoring JSON, provider trace, and response text was archived and hashed (execution/scoring/*.json; execution/provider_calls/*.json; execution/responses/*.txt). Representative scoring JSONs and their SHA‑256 hashes are included in the manuscript artifacts (e.g., execution/scoring/task-000001-guarded.json SHA‑256 = 3055f874...).

Statistical plan for degenerate outcomes. The preregistered power calculation targeted a baseline failure rate ≈ 0.20; however, the analysis contract used exact McNemar two‑sided inference and a paired bootstrap percentile CI (10,000 resamples, seed=1729). When no discordant pairs are observed, exact McNemar yields p=1.00 and the bootstrap percentile CI degenerates to the observed point mass (here [0.00,0.00]). We report both the exact test and the bootstrap CI as the correct inferential description under the observed data.
sections.results:
Execution provenance and accounting. Planned episodes: 400 (two arms × 200 tasks). Completed episodes: 400. Model calls used: 200 (single shared initial generator per task; no repair calls were invoked). No provider/infrastructure failures compromised the run. Key artifact fingerprints: execution/raw_results.jsonl (SHA‑256 = 3dfbe1b6580c9df4...), execution/model_configuration.json (gpt-5-mini requested; SHA‑256 = 1acce92558edeb13...), execution/transformation_manifest.json (SHA‑256 = 79c91155...), and the master prompt archive provenance/master_prompt.txt (SHA‑256 = 1872df1e...). Deterministic reconciliation confirmed consistent episode accounting and no cross‑condition cache reuse (analysis/deterministic_reconciliation.json).

Primary confirmatory outcome (artifact‑grounded). Complete paired count: 200 paired tasks. Baseline validator passes = 200/200; guarded validator passes = 200/200. Paired contingency (guarded × baseline): n11 = 200, n10 = 0, n01 = 0, n00 = 0 (analysis/paired_contingency_table.csv SHA‑256 = 7bc1bd2a...). Paired difference (guarded − baseline) = 0.00. Exact McNemar two‑sided p = 1.00. Paired bootstrap (10,000 resamples, seed=1729) 95% percentile CI = [0.00,0.00] (analysis/analysis_log.jsonl). The guarded repair pathway was never invoked: repair_applied=false in every guarded scoring JSON (execution/scoring/*.json).

Representative diagnostics. Each per‑task scoring JSON records normalized_configuration, parsed_command_count, observed_touched_field_count, difficulty metadata, and final_state snapshot. For example, execution/scoring/task-000001-guarded.json (SHA‑256 = 3055f874...) shows parsed_command_count=4, observed_touched_field_count=3, validator.valid=true and provides the final simulated device state snapshot. A small representative set (embedded in execution/task_manifest.jsonl) lists medium/hard/very_hard annotations for several tasks; those per‑task entries are archived for deterministic aggregation. The full per‑task difficulty metadata can be deterministically re‑aggregated by replaying execution/scoring/*.json (artifacts present but the aggregated counts were not preregistered and therefore not computed during run-time).
sections.discussion:
Why repairs were not invoked (artifact‑grounded explanation). Three archived, non‑contradicted facts explain the null/ceiling outcome: (1) Inclusion required validator coverage: task selection filtered to intents the validator supports (execution/task_manifest.jsonl SHA‑256 = f1d447b7...), biasing the pool toward intents the verifier can assess; (2) The requested LLM (gpt-5-mini) produced candidates that satisfied the explicit workflow constraints embedded in the task payloads (per‑task normalized_configuration equals the reference in execution/scoring/*.json); and (3) The shared_initial_generation design fixes the generator output across arms, preventing generator adaptation; consequently no initial candidate failed validation and the repair path was never exercised. These statements are verifiable from the archived scoring JSONs and provider traces (execution/scoring/*.json and execution/provider_calls/*.json) and from the execution manifest (execution/execution_manifest.json).

Statistical interpretation and practical implications. The exact test and bootstrap CI correctly describe the observed data: a paired difference of 0.00 with degenerate CI [0.00,0.00] indicates no evidence of a verifier marginal benefit under the sampled regime. This is a ceiling/null empirical outcome specific to the tested model/task/validator combination and the shared_initial estimand. It does not imply verifiers are unnecessary in failure‑rich or production settings. Practically, confirmatory tests of verifier utility should avoid ceiling regimes: (i) sample or construct failure‑rich tasks (historical misconfigurations, adversarial boundary cases), (ii) evaluate multiple generator strengths (weaker LLMs or constrained modes), and/or (iii) alter the estimand to an interactive generator–verifier loop that allows regeneration in response to verifier feedback. Our archived artifacts contain the per‑task difficulty and validator coverage metadata needed to design such follow‑ups deterministically (execution/scoring/*.json and execution/task_manifest.jsonl). Researchers can replay the run and recompute an alternative estimand by permitting generator regeneration (the run archive contains all prompts, responses, and hashes required for that replay). 

Threats to validity. Internal: shared_initial_generation isolates verifier marginality but prevents closed‑loop evaluation; selection filter required validator coverage (introduces selection bias toward verifier‑handleable intents). Construct: validator fidelity constrains what we term a 'regression'—the observed 100% pass rate depends on validator coverage of real regression modes. External: single requested_model (gpt-5-mini) and synthetic/deterministic task pool limit generalizability. Conclusion validity: observed baseline=0.0 invalidated the preregistered power assumptions; the exact paired inference and bootstrap reflect observed uncertainty correctly.
sections.conclusion: Under the preregistered paired contract and deterministic task selection, both arms produced 200/200 validator‑compliant applies; the repair path was never invoked and the paired difference was exactly 0.00 (McNemar p=1.00; bootstrap 95% CI = [0.00,0.00]). This ceiling/null result is reproducible from the provided artifacts (raw_results.jsonl SHA‑256 = 3dfbe1b6580c9df4...) and does not contradict the operational value of verifiers in failure‑rich settings. We therefore recommend that future confirmatory evaluations intentionally sample failure‑rich tasks, vary generator strengths, and/or measure interactive generator–verifier closed‑loop estimands. All execution artifacts, scoring traces, and the master prompt reference (provenance/master_prompt.txt; SHA‑256 = 1872df1e...) are released for replay and independent audit.

limitations: Single‑model evaluation (requested_model = gpt-5-mini) — results do not generalize to other LLMs without additional experiments.

Synthetic deterministic task pool and the preregistered inclusion rule (validator coverage required) bias the confirmatory sample toward intents the validator can assess; this selection limits external validity to production intent distributions that include emergent or historical misconfigurations.

Construct validity is tied to deterministic_netops_validator_v5 fidelity; if the validator lacks coverage for real regression failure modes, the binary outcome conflates true safety with validator reach.

Design constraint: shared_initial_generation fixes generator outputs across arms and prevents generator adaptation; the experiment therefore measures verifier marginality on fixed candidates, not closed‑loop generator–verifier improvement.
Observed ceiling (baseline success = 100%) rendered the preregistered power calculation inapplicable; inference is descriptive and artifact‑grounded for the tested regime.
